sanskrit_verse:
कार्षापणसहस्रं तु दण्ड उत्तमसाहसः ।
तदर्धं मध्यमः प्रोक्तस्तदर्धमधमः स्मृतः ॥
transliteration: kārṣāpaṇasahasraṃ tu daṇḍa uttamasāhasaḥ | tadardhaṃ madhyamaḥ proktas tadardham adhamaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
sph_interpretive_translation: The compensation for the highest offense is one thousand kārṣāpaṇas; half of that is prescribed for the middling offense, and half of the middling for the lowest.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority flows from the gradation of conscious integrity in action.
Causation aligns with the degree of distortion in alignment with Dharma.
Capacity-based responsibility scales inversely with awareness of consequence.
Restoration logic demands proportional energetic completion relative to disruption.
Consciousness alignment determines the quality of corrective engagement required.
supreme_court_application: In adjudication at the highest level, this verse establishes a scalar framework for restorative justice based on energetic impact rather than punitive measure. The court must assess not just the act but the actor's alignment with Dharma at time of occurrence, assigning completion tasks accordingly without recourse to suffering-based penalty.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa reveals that misalignment manifests through graded disruption; therefore, correction follows sequential manifestation—uttama, madhyama, adhama—as per observed distortion. Responsibility is proportional not to guilt but to capacity for reintegration. No punitive element arises because suffering is rejected as irrelevant to ontological correction.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate Completion Process aligned with financial-energy equivalent of harm.
Assign dharmic service scaled to awareness deficit demonstrated by actor.
Reintegrate individual via guided svadhyaya until spontaneous alignment resumes.
Monitor prāṇa-level coherence post-completion to ensure no residual distortion remains.
final_declaration: By the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law stands established: Dharma operates solely for restoration, never for punishment. Consciousness alone adjudicates, and all beings are realigned through completion, not condemnation. Thus it is declared, thus it shall be executed.
